spindle.observe.DeliveryGuarantee.title: DeliveryGuarantee
spindle.observe.DeliveryGuarantee.description: How many times an event binding's command may run for one event, as the binding's `delivery:` writes it. The words are ESS's (`Delivery` in ESS 0.90.0 `crates/specify/ess-domain/src/binding.rs`, carried on `ResolvedBinding::delivery`), and Spindle publishes them unchanged. `at_least_once`: ESS lets the command run again, so it must be idempotent. `at_most_once`: one send and no redelivery. Neither is exactly once. Spindle sends each event to a binding once under either word: the receiving component acknowledges an `at_least_once` envelope, and no runtime path resends one whose acknowledgement is overdue (`spindle_channel::Sender::redeliver` exists, and the host never calls it), so the conformance target answers ESS's redelivery step unsupported (`crates/spindle-conformance/src/target.rs`). A command that does not take effect may still run again where the binding retries (`BindingDelivery.attempts`). In either, Spindle sends nothing for an event before the state that published it is durable (`crates/spindle-channel/src/lib.rs`).
